body: Without credentials, the filter must give a name or at least one `@property`. Unsupported keys or operators fail instead of silently broadening the search. - Allowed keys are `repo`, `name`, `path`, `type` and `@property`. `type`, when supplied, must be `file`. - A condition is a plain value or an object with exactly one `$eq`. Only `name` and `path` also allow `$match`; arrays, nested operator values and multiple operators are refused. - `*` matches any run and `?` one character. Other punctuation is literal. The native and formal contrasts cover ordinary ASCII text without newlines; ICU character behavior outside that scope is open.

body: Anonymous search keeps only results matching the repository, name, path and every required property, then takes the first result with the greatest `lastUpdated` text. An equal timestamp keeps the earlier result; no match is an error. - Each required property must occur among that result's property values. Missing or scalar property data does not satisfy it. - A root-level artifact uses `.` for path matching. Its returned download path omits that dot folder. - With credentials, IPM asks AQL to sort by decreasing update time and takes result zero. It does not sort or recheck that response locally. Correct filtering and order on this path depend on the server; reversing a disposable server's response reverses IPM's choice.

A public byte endpoint succeeds. - This is a confirmed mismatch in the credential handoff, recorded as C:D17. HTTP status must be 200; success in search does not establish permission to fetch the artifact.

body: Activate reuses an existing local artifact folder without checking its contents or contacting the server. Export calls the download helper even when that folder exists. - The byte helper fetches the response, but does not overwrite a temporary file with the same returned filename. Its previous bytes can therefore be reused even after a newer response arrives. File existence is not a freshness check. - Successful copies overlay the destination: equal names are overwritten and unrelated target files remain. Other exported resources are outside this resource's destination and remain untouched. - The caller builds that export destination from the module or dependency location and the resource's relative path. The processor does not independently choose the package root.

body: A missing `ARTI_SERVER` is an error outside developer mode and a warning with no download in developer mode. Developer mode also warns and skips anonymous search or fetch failures, but does not suppress authenticated failures or an extraction exception. - Skipping does not create an artifact folder. Activate returns success without copying if the folder is still absent. Export still tries its copy, so the same skip does not by itself establish export success. - Extraction and copies may leave files when a later step fails. A database rollback does not compensate those effects. No general filesystem atomicity is claimed.

body: An archive read error should fail extraction and the consuming download. Success must not hide a reported stream error. - Known gap C:D18: on the tested IRIS provider, a non-gzip byte sequence produces an empty read with an error status. The tar reader ignores that status and treats the empty header as completion; the archive wrapper then returns success. Both ordinary and developer-mode anonymous downloads can succeed with an empty artifact folder. - A gzip stream containing a nonempty header with a bad checksum is refused. A valid archive extracts its file. These neighbors distinguish the defect from a policy that rejects every empty archive. - The formal contract covers the first-header decision under the observed gzip/header provider. It does not verify gzip decoding, checksum arithmetic, PAX records, path traversal or every extraction write.

body: When should an existing artifact folder or same-named temporary file be refreshed? - Owner: IPM maintainers and module authors. The code deliberately reuses a local folder during Activate, but no accepted cache identity or expiry rule was found. - Working assumption: preserve observed reuse and disclose that it gives no freshness guarantee. Alternatives are immutable digest-addressed files, explicit refresh, or validating the cached bytes against the selected artifact. - This decision affects reproducible installs and exports. Do not remove local/offline reuse as part of an authentication repair.

body:
Should artifact copies refuse protected installation folders as FileCopy does?

- Owner: IPM maintainers and instance administrators. The processor calls the shared warning before Activate's copy; it does not call FileCopy's deletion guard. No protected system folder was modified in this run.
- Working assumption: disclose the warning boundary without promising protection. Alternatives are a common refusal rule, an explicit operator override, or retaining warning-only behavior.
- Archive path safety, partial copies and compensation remain open. A successful copy under `/tmp` settles none of these policies.

body: `sync []` brings changed files from disk into developer-mode modules without a full reload. It finds files changed since the last load or sync by their hash and recompiles only what is out of date. - With no module, it syncs every developer-mode module in dependency order. - `-delete` also removes items whose files were deleted, and `-test` runs test classes that changed. - `load -skip-sync` leaves recording the hashes to the next `sync`. - A failed sync with an existing baseline keeps its retry mark. The next sync retries that file even if its bytes equal the stored baseline. - A failed compile, load or reload outside sync can change server code without setting that mark. Reverting to exact baseline bytes can then make sync report nothing to do while the server keeps the edited code; this is the separate outside-sync premise and P:F-SYNC-1. - A test failure after successful sync activation happens after hash commit and does not undo it.

body: A test resource must declare exactly one of Class and Package. Its phase list matches phase names without regard to case; a Class resource ignores Suite and Case path selectors. - A Package resource uses Suite if that key is defined, otherwise Case. Suite slashes become dots. Even a defined empty Suite takes precedence over Case and leaves path filtering off. - Package selection compares raw prefixes in either direction, so package `A` can be selected by `AB`. Changed-class ownership is stricter: it accepts `A` or `A.` followed by a class name, and rejects `AB`. - These are two different readers. Selecting a test resource does not establish that sync assigns a changed class to it, and converting a file path does not itself establish class ownership.

body: As built, the document exporter overwrites the deployed-item helper's returned error with success before deciding whether to export source. It removes missing items and may return success with fewer items, so it is not proof that a discarded item or helper error will be caught. Source files, final project contents and command status must be assessed separately. - The proposed repair is to preserve the helper status. It has not been applied to the product. An error after a provider's partial write may leave that write; no compensation is inferred.

body: IPM writes the permanent record when the action starts and keeps the in-progress record in IRISTEMP, which a rollback does not undo. When the action ends, IPM copies the result to the permanent record. For a top-level action started outside any transaction, both writes happen outside the action's transaction, so its rollback cannot undo them. - Process loss and instance restart differ. In a checked SIGKILL schedule, temporary progress and the initial permanent row remained. After a whole-instance restart, the temporary row was gone and the durable initial permanent row remained unfinished. - These observations require the checked IRISTEMP mapping and durable database. They do not establish power-loss durability, replication or every caller-transaction schedule. [Paired native and formal evidence](../../uplift/consolidated/iter2/boundaries/REPORT.md).

body: Each record holds: - `Action`: `load`, `install`, `uninstall` or `update`. - `Package`: the module name. It is empty only if the action failed before any name was known, such as a load of a folder without a valid manifest. A refusal after IPM read the manifest records the name. - `Version`: the module version. Until the version is known it is stored as `0.0.0-0` and shown as ``. - Source name, type and details: the repository an install came from. They are empty for load and uninstall, and listings show `n/a` for any action other than install. - `TimeStart` and `TimeEnd`: the end time is empty while the action runs or after it ended abnormally. - `UserName`: the user who started the action. - `Success`: the action's status. It is `0` while the action is in progress. - `Committed`: whether the action kept changes ([committed](#history.committed)). - `CommandString`: the command as typed. - `Phases`: the [phase entries](#history.phases).

body: For `load`, `install` and `update`, `Committed` shows whether the action kept any changes, either by a commit or by writing outside a transaction. An uncommitted action wrote nothing or was rolled back. - A successful action is committed, unless a parent load's rollback later undoes it. A dependency undone that way reads uncommitted. - A failure rolled back in full is not committed. This includes a developer-mode failure before its [first commit](load.g5.md#load.outcome.dev.early-failure). - A developer-mode failure after its first commit is committed. - A failure with `-DNoTransaction=1` or `-DNoJournal=1` is committed once the action has started writing. - A refusal before anything is written is not committed, in any mode. - `Committed` describes database writes; it does not promise to undo copied files, lock files, pip effects or CPF changes. The property comment and maintainer history design review settle this field meaning (P DEC-HIST-5). - Inherited [side-effects question](#history.committed.side-effects) is retained as an alias for that resolved interpretation. After a post-commit error the record can be committed and unsuccessful. - Unresolved Q-26: [Should a parent record count writes kept only by its NoJournal dependency?](#history.committed.escaped-dependency)

body: `-D=` filters records, and several filters must all match. - A value can use `*` as a wildcard, or start with `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=` or `<>`. - `history schema` lists the columns that can be filtered. - Versions are filtered by part, such as `Version_Major`. - Filters work the same way for `find` and `delete`. - As built, `ConstructSQLWhere` walks keys in IRIS collation order and stops at the first absent value or name outside `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*`. It keeps earlier predicates and ignores that key and every later one. - An underscore column such as `Version_Major` can therefore leave no predicate: an unmatched `Version_Major=99` deleted all three seeded identities. A valid `Package=del-b` or `Success=0` deleted only its matches. - An unknown alphanumeric column raises SQL error; `find` can hide that error behind an empty successful listing while delete throws. These are failures of the rule, not permitted filtering behavior (G:D2).

body: May `history delete` or the daily [purge](#history.retention) remove the record of an action that is still running, and what should that action's final write do then? - Provisional answer: a delete or purge may remove any matching record, and the running action must still finish normally whether or not its record comes back. - Reason: no source covers this case. Deleting is an explicit user choice, and the log must not make a package change fail. - Alternative: skip records of running actions, or always write the final result back. - As built, deleting an accessible active twin before final persistence leaves the row absent even when Finalize and PersistToTwin return success. - A transaction-locked twin has a different checked schedule: delete waits, final persistence runs, the transaction releases its lock, delete completes, then temporary-object close recreates the same ID with its finalized successful result. A successful delete is not cancellation of the remaining writer. - The [paired final-reader receipts and Verus schedule contract](../../uplift/consolidated/iter2/boundaries/REPORT.md) refute a general no-resurrection claim. They cover two schedules, not all lock timeouts, interleavings or cross-namespace behavior. The alternatives above remain an owner policy question.

body: What a failed load keeps depends on how it ran. | How the load ran | What a failure keeps | |---|---| | Normal mode, in a transaction | No module data. The whole load, including dependencies loaded for it, is rolled back. | | Developer mode, in a transaction | Depends on when it fails. See [developer-mode commits](#load.outcome.dev). | | `-DNoTransaction=1` or `-DNoJournal=1` | Everything written before the failure. | - A [refusal](#load.refusal) keeps no module data in any mode. The requirements check is the open exception. - A process that dies mid-load ends like a failure at that point. The open transaction is rolled back, so the table applies, and with `-DNoTransaction=1` or `-DNoJournal=1` nothing is rolled back and the namespace may be left inconsistent. - Whether a dependency's own `` transaction flags change this is open: `NoJournal` ([dependency defaults](../concepts/transactions-and-dev-mode.g5.md#transaction.flag-sources.dependency-defaults)) and `NoTransaction` ([dependency NoTransaction](../concepts/transactions-and-dev-mode.g5.md#transaction.flag-sources.dependency-no-transaction)). - Files and other changes outside the database follow the [rollback scope](../concepts/transactions-and-dev-mode.g5.md#transaction.rollback-scope). - The [history record](history.g5.md#history.committed) shows whether anything was kept. After a dying process, see [record](history.g5.md#history.record). - This rollback rule applies to database writes made before the final commit, with journaling enabled. A failed after-install message or cleanup after that commit returns an error with the module kept ([late errors](#load.status.after-commit)). - Child flags are resolved separately on each activation. An absent parent key permits the child's own default; a defined parent value, including zero, wins. - Child `NoTransaction` skips its own `TSTART` and leaves an existing parent transaction open. Child `NoJournal` can make its writes survive parent rollback. Their intended policy stays in the linked child questions. - Class descriptors and usable code are separate outcomes. After two-resource compile failure, ordinary rollback removes both classes. - Without transactions, or after the developer commit, both descriptors may remain while only the first class runs. This relies on the observed IRIS compiler behavior, not on a proof of the compiler.

body: A `.modules` folder in the module root serves as a temporary repository for that load's dependencies. IPM removes this temporary repository when loading finishes, even after an error. - IPM creates none when the folder is missing or another repository already uses that folder. That other repository stays. - The temporary repository takes the first unused name `ipm-temp-modules-N`. - A dependency's own `.modules` folder gets the same treatment while that dependency loads. - Which copy of a dependency wins is owned by [search order](../concepts/repositories.g5.md#repo.search-order). Whether the `.modules` copy should win a tie is [open](#load.dependencies.local-repo.precedence). - Cache creation failure can leave no row but retain its allocated id in the manager. Cleanup may warn about that missing row (C:D2). At the top-level cleanup call the module can already be committed; at a dependency call the parent rolls back, retaining its first manifest commit only in developer mode. - A higher candidate version wins before repository order. Equal versions choose the older repository id in the native observations; temporary sort position does not force local priority (C:Q1).

body: `-env` takes `;`-separated JSON files of settings for the module, merges them and replaces `${VAR}` with environment values. The module reads them with `%IPM.General.EnvironmentConfig:GetArg`, and a missing file is an error. - Files merge in order. A later value replaces an earlier one, and nested objects merge key by key. - Every command that runs module phases starts from an empty configuration and loads only its own `-env` files.
